drivingQuestion: What does the mishna mean by oref, and what does its closing clause — that what is valid for slaughter is invalid for pinching — come to exclude?
outcomeNote: עורף in the mishna is settled as ממול עורף; the sons of R' Ḥiyya are read as אף מחזיר and defended by assigning them to the view that drawing back and forth invalidates pinching; R' Yirmeya's reading of the closing clause stands, and Rav Kahana's ״זו היא מצותה״ is emended to ״אף זו היא מצותה״.

segments.he: גְּמָ׳ מַאי עוֹרֶף? אִילֵימָא עוֹרֶף מַמָּשׁ, מַאי אִרְיָא שׁוֹחֵט? אֲפִילּוּ מוֹלֵק נָמֵי! ״מִמּוּל עׇרְפּוֹ״ אָמַר רַחֲמָנָא, וְלֹא עׇרְפּוֹ. אֶלָּא מַאי עוֹרֶף? מִמּוּל עוֹרֶף, כִּדְקָתָנֵי סֵיפָא: כׇּל הָעוֹרֶף כָּשֵׁר לִמְלִיקָה.
segments.en: «GEMARA:» With regard to the statement in the mishna: One who slaughters an animal from the oref, its slaughter is not valid, the Gemara asks: «What» is the meaning of «oref? If we say» that the reference is to the «actual occipital bone» at the rear of the skull, «why» does this halakha apply «specifically» to one who «slaughters» from the oref? «Even» if one «pinches» a bird offering from the oref it would «also» not be valid, as «the Merciful One states:» “Pinch off its head «adjacent to its oref”» (Leviticus 5:8), at the nape beneath the occipital bone, «and not its oref. Rather, what» is the «oref» mentioned in the mishna? It is «adjacent to the oref,» the back of the neck below the occipital bone, «as it is taught» in «the latter clause» of the mishna: «The entire nape is valid for pinching.»

segments.he: מְנָהָנֵי מִילֵּי, דְּתָנוּ רַבָּנַן: ״מִמּוּל עׇרְפּוֹ״ – מוּל הָרוֹאֶה אֶת הָעוֹרֶף, וְכֵן הוּא אוֹמֵר: ״וְהוּא יֹשֵׁב מִמֻּלִי״, וְאוֹמֵר: ״כִּי פָנוּ אֵלַי עֹרֶף וְלֹא פָנִים״. מַאי וְאוֹמֵר? וְכִי תֵּימָא: עוֹרֶף גּוּפֵיהּ לָא יָדְעִינַן הֵיכָא, דְּנִדַּע מוּל דִּידֵיהּ הֵיכָא – תָּא שְׁמַע: ״כִּי פָנוּ אֵלַי עֹרֶף וְלֹא פָנִים״, מִכְּלָל דְּעוֹרֶף לַהֲדֵי פָּנִים.
segments.en: The Gemara asks: «From where are these matters» derived? They are derived «as the Sages taught» in a baraita: In the phrase «“adjacent to [mimmul] its oref,” adjacent» means a place «that sees the oref» and not the oref itself. «And likewise,» the verse «states: “And they reside adjacent to me [mimmuli]”» (Numbers 22:5); «and» the verse «states: “For they have turned their oref unto Me, and not their face”» (Jeremiah 2:27). The Gemara asks: «What» is added by the latter proof, introduced with the term: «And» the verse «states?» The Gemara answers: «And if you would say, we do not know where the oref itself» is, so «that we will know where adjacent to it is, come» and «hear: “For they have turned their oref unto Me, and not their face,”» from which it may be ascertained «by inference that the oref is opposite the face,» at the rear of the head.

segments.he: אָמְרִי בְּנֵי רַבִּי חִיָּיא: מִצְוַת מְלִיקָה מַחֲזִיר סִימָנִים לַאֲחוֹרֵי הָעוֹרֶף וּמוֹלֵק. אִיכָּא דְּאָמְרִי: אַף מַחְזִיר, וְאִיכָּא דְּאָמְרִי: מַחְזִיר דַּוְקָא.
segments.en: § «The sons of Rabbi Ḥiyya say:» How is «the mitzva of pinching» of a bird offering performed? «One moves» the two «simanim» that must be severed in ritual slaughter, i.e., the windpipe and the gullet, «behind the nape and pinches.» There is a dispute among the Sages with regard to the meaning of the statement. «There are» those «who say:» The mitzva ab initio is to pinch through the spinal column first and then pinch the windpipe and the gullet, and one may «even move» the simanim to behind the nape and pinch. «And there are» those «who say:» The mitzva is «specifically» to «move» the simanim behind the nape and pinch.

segments.he: וּמִסְתַּבְּרָא כְּמַאן דְּאָמַר אַף מַחְזִיר, מִמַּאי? מִדְּקָתָנֵי: הַשּׁוֹחֵט מִן הָעוֹרֶף – שְׁחִיטָתוֹ פְּסוּלָה, הַמּוֹלֵק מִן הָעוֹרֶף – מְלִיקָתוֹ כְּשֵׁרָה,
segments.en: The Gemara notes: «And it is reasonable according to the one who says: One may even move» the simanim behind the nape. «From where» does one draw that conclusion? It is «from» the fact «that» the mishna «teaches: One who slaughters from the nape» of the neck, «his slaughter is not valid. One who pinches from the nape» of the neck, «his pinching is valid.»

segments.he: וְאִי סָלְקָא דַעְתָּךְ מַחְזִיר דַּוְקָא, מַאי אִירְיָא מוֹלֵק? אֲפִילּוּ שׁוֹחֵט נָמֵי! אֶלָּא לָאו שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ אַף מַחְזִיר, וּמַתְנִיתִין בִּדְלָא אַהְדַּר.
segments.en: «And if it enters your mind that» the mitzva is «specifically» to «move» the simanim behind the nape and pinch them, «why» did the tanna say «specifically» that if one «pinches» in this manner it is valid? «Even» if «one slaughters» from the nape in this manner the slaughter would be valid. «Rather,» must one «not conclude from it» that the proper understanding is: One may «even move» the simanim behind the nape and pinch, «and the mishna is» referring to a case «where one did not move» the simanim behind the nape.

segments.he: אָמַר רַבִּי יַנַּאי: יְקַבְּלוּ הָרוֹבִין אֶת תְּשׁוּבָתָן, דְּקָתָנֵי: נִמְצָא כָּשֵׁר בִּשְׁחִיטָה – פָּסוּל בִּמְלִיקָה, כָּשֵׁר בִּמְלִיקָה – פָּסוּל בִּשְׁחִיטָה. לְמַעוֹטֵי מַאי? לָאו לְמַעוֹטֵי מַחֲזִיר סִימָנִין לַאֲחוֹרֵי הָעוֹרֶף, דְּלָא?
segments.en: «Rabbi Yannai says: The young ones [rovin],» the sons of Rabbi Ḥiyya, «shall receive their response» that rejects their statement from «that» which «is taught» in the mishna: «It is found that» that which is «valid for slaughter» is «not valid for pinching and» that which is «valid for pinching» is «not valid for slaughter. What» does this statement serve «to exclude?» Does it «not» serve «to exclude» the case where «one moves the simanim behind the nape,» teaching «that» it is valid only for slaughter and «not» for pinching?

segments.he: אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה: לָא, לְמַעוֹטֵי שֵׁן וְצִפּוֹרֶן. שֵׁן וְצִפּוֹרֶן בְּהֶדְיָא קָתָנֵי לְהוּ.
segments.en: «Rabba bar bar Ḥana said: No,» perhaps it serves «to exclude» one who uses «a tooth or a fingernail» that is not detached, which are valid for pinching and not valid for slaughter. The Gemara objects: That could not be, as the tanna «teaches explicitly» the case of «a tooth and a fingernail» in a mishna (15b), and there was no need to repeat it.

segments.he: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַבִּי יִרְמְיָה: לְמַעוֹטֵי מוֹלִיךְ וּמֵבִיא. הָנִיחָא לְמַאן דְּאָמַר מוֹלִיךְ וּמֵבִיא בִּמְלִיקָה – פָּסוּל, אֶלָּא לְמַאן דְּאָמַר כָּשֵׁר, מַאי אִיכָּא לְמֵימַר? בְּנֵי רַבִּי חִיָּיא סָבְרִי לַהּ כְּמַאן דְּאָמַר מוֹלִיךְ וּמֵבִיא בִּמְלִיקָה – פָּסוּל.
segments.en: «Rather, Rabbi Yirmeya said:» The statement of the mishna: That which is valid for slaughter is not valid for pinching, serves «to exclude drawing back and forth.» One who pinches may not cut the simanim by drawing his fingernail back and forth. Rather, he must press and cut them in one motion. The Gemara asks: «This works out well according to the one who says: Drawing back and forth for pinching is not valid, but according to the one who says:» It is «valid, what is there to say?» The Gemara answers: «The sons of Rabbi Ḥiyya hold in accordance with the one who says: Drawing back and forth for pinching is not valid.»

segments.he: אָמַר רַב כָּהֲנָא: מִצְוַת מְלִיקָה קוֹצֵץ וְיוֹרֵד, וְזוֹ הִיא מִצְוָתָהּ. סָבַר רַבִּי אָבִין לְמֵימַר: קוֹצֵץ וְיוֹרֵד – אִין, מוֹלִיךְ וּמֵבִיא – לָא. אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי יִרְמְיָה: כׇּל שֶׁכֵּן דְּמוֹלִיךְ וּמֵבִיא בִּמְלִיקָה כָּשֵׁר, וּמַאי זוֹ הִיא מִצְוָתָהּ? אֵימָא: אַף זוֹ הִיא מִצְוָתָהּ.
segments.en: «Rav Kahana says: The mitzva of pinching» is that «one cuts» with his fingernail from the nape «and continues downward, and that is its mitzva. Rabbi Avin thought to say: Cuts and continues downward, yes; draws back and forth, no. Rabbi Yirmeya said to him: All the more so that drawing back and forth for pinching is valid.» The Gemara asks: «And what» is the meaning of the phrase: «That is its mitzva,» which indicates that it is specifically in that manner? The Gemara answers: «Say» that it means: «That too is its mitzva.»

moves.summary: The Gemara asks what the mishna of the preceding unit means by oref
moves.about: what the term עורף denotes in the mishna's rule that slaughter from the oref is invalid

moves.summary: Floats the reading that oref means the actual occipital bone
moves.about: the Torah requires pinching adjacent to the nape and not at the occipital bone itself

moves.cueHe: מאי אריא שוחט? אפילו מולק נמי!
moves.summary: Knocks down the floated reading: on it, pinching there would be invalid too, since the verse says adjacent to its oref and not its oref
moves.about: whether עורף in the mishna means the occipital bone itself — rejected, since pinching there would be invalid too and the mishna singles out slaughter

moves.summary: Answers that oref in the mishna means the area adjacent to the nape
moves.about: the mishna's עורף means the area adjacent to the nape, below the occipital bone, not the bone itself

moves.cueHe: כדקתני סיפא: כל העורף כשר למליקה
moves.summary: Supports the answer from the mishna's own latter clause, which speaks of the whole nape
moves.about: the mishna's own latter clause, that the entire nape is valid for pinching, shows עורף names a broad area rather than the bone

moves.summary: Asks for the scriptural warrant of that reading
moves.about: the scriptural warrant for reading ממול ערפו as the place that faces the nape rather than the nape itself

moves.summary: Adduces a baraita as the source
moves.about: a baraita expounding ממול ערפו is adduced as the source for the reading just given

moves.summary: The baraita expounds mimmul as the place that sees the nape
moves.about: מול in the verse denotes the place that sees the nape, not the nape itself

moves.summary: Brings a verse showing mimmul means facing
moves.about: proof that ממול means facing or opposite, from ״והוא יושב ממולי״

moves.cueHe: ואומר: ״כי פנו אלי עורף ולא פנים״
moves.summary: Brings a second verse setting nape against face
moves.about: a second prooftext locating the nape opposite the face

moves.summary: Asks what the second prooftext adds
moves.about: why the baraita needs the second prooftext introduced by ואומר once the first has been brought

moves.cueHe: וכי תימא: עורף גופיה לא ידעינן היכא
moves.summary: Answers that without it we would not know where the nape itself is
moves.about: the second verse is required because without it we would not know where the nape itself is, and so could not locate what faces it

moves.summary: Infers from the verse that the nape lies opposite the face
moves.about: the verse's contrast of nape and face shows that the nape lies opposite the face, at the rear of the head

moves.cueHe: אמרי בני רבי חייא: מצות מליקה
moves.summary: The sons of R' Ḥiyya state that the mitzva of pinching is to move the simanim behind the nape and pinch
moves.about: their ruling means one may also move the simanim behind the nape and pinch, the mitzva ab initio being to cut through the spine first

moves.summary: Some read their words as permitting, not requiring, moving the simanim
moves.about: whether the sons of R' Ḥiyya's rule that one moves the simanim behind the nape and pinches makes that manner merely also valid or strictly required

moves.summary: Others read their words as requiring specifically that one move the simanim
moves.about: their ruling means the mitzva is specifically to move the simanim behind the nape and pinch there

moves.summary: The Gemara judges the permissive reading the more reasonable
moves.about: the mishna's rule that slaughter from the nape is invalid while pinching from the nape is valid

moves.summary: Cites the mishna's pairing of invalid slaughter and valid pinching at the nape
moves.about: the mishna's contrast between invalid slaughter and valid pinching at the nape makes the permissive reading the more reasonable one

moves.summary: Asks on what basis
moves.about: on what basis the permissive reading is judged the more reasonable

moves.cueHe: ואי סלקא דעתך מחזיר דוקא, מאי אירייא מולק?
moves.summary: On the requiring reading, slaughter after moving the simanim would be valid too, so the mishna would not single out pinching
moves.about: if moving the simanim behind the nape were strictly required, slaughter performed that way would be valid too, so the mishna would not have singled out pinching

moves.cueHe: אלא לאו שמע מינה אף מחזיר
moves.summary: Concludes that the permissive reading is right
moves.about: the mishna's wording shows that the sons of R' Ḥiyya meant one may also move the simanim behind the nape

moves.summary: Establishes that the mishna's invalidation of slaughter at the nape speaks where the simanim were not moved back
moves.about: the mishna invalidating slaughter from the nape speaks of a case where one did not move the simanim back

moves.cueHe: אמר רבי ינאי: יקבלו הרובין את תשובתן
moves.summary: R' Yannai objects to the sons of R' Ḥiyya from the mishna's closing clause
moves.about: whether the mishna's closing clause refutes their account of how the mitzva of pinching is performed

moves.cueHe: למעוטי מאי? לאו למעוטי מחזיר סימנין לאחורי העורף
moves.summary: Reads the closing clause as excluding moving the simanim behind the nape
moves.about: the mishna's closing clause that what is valid for slaughter is invalid for pinching and vice versa

moves.cueHe: אמר רבה בר בר חנה: לא, למעוטי שן וצפורן
moves.summary: Rejects R' Yannai's proposed exclusion and offers tooth and fingernail instead
moves.about: what the mishna's closing clause comes to exclude

moves.summary: Objects that tooth and fingernail are already taught explicitly in an earlier mishna
moves.about: tooth and fingernail are already taught explicitly in an earlier mishna, so the closing clause cannot have been needed for them

moves.cueHe: אלא אמר רבי ירמיה: למעוטי מוליך ומביא
moves.summary: R' Yirmeya replaces the reading: the clause excludes drawing the fingernail back and forth
moves.about: what the mishna's closing clause comes to exclude, now that tooth and fingernail are ruled out

moves.cueHe: הניחא למאן דאמר מוליך ומביא במליקה – פסול
moves.summary: Presses that his reading holds only for the view that drawing back and forth invalidates pinching
moves.about: his reading of the clause works only for the view that drawing back and forth invalidates pinching, and not for the view that it is valid

moves.cueHe: בני רבי חייא סברי לה כמאן דאמר
moves.summary: Answers that the sons of R' Ḥiyya hold like the view that invalidates drawing back and forth
moves.target: unnamed:מאן דאמר מוליך ומביא במליקה פסול
moves.about: the sons of R' Ḥiyya reason from the view that drawing back and forth invalidates pinching, which is how the difficulty is answered

moves.cueHe: אמר רב כהנא: מצות מליקה קוצץ ויורד
moves.summary: Rav Kahana states that pinching is done by cutting and continuing downward, and that is its mitzva
moves.about: Rav Kahana's description of how the mitzva of pinching is performed is adduced on this topic

moves.cueHe: סבר רבי אבין למימר: קוצץ ויורד – אין, מוליך ומביא – לא
moves.summary: R' Avin floats the reading that Rav Kahana excludes drawing back and forth
moves.about: whether Rav Kahana's ״וזו היא מצותה״ excludes drawing the fingernail back and forth

moves.cueHe: אמר ליה רבי ירמיה: כל שכן דמוליך ומביא במליקה כשר
moves.summary: R' Yirmeya rejects that reading: a fortiori, drawing back and forth is valid
moves.about: whether Rav Kahana's ruling excludes drawing back and forth or shows all the more so that it is valid

moves.summary: Asks what Rav Kahana's exclusive-sounding phrase then means
moves.about: what Rav Kahana's phrase ״זו היא מצותה״ means, given that it appears to restrict the mitzva to that manner alone

moves.summary: Emends the phrase to that too is its mitzva
moves.about: his words are to be read as ״אף זו היא מצותה״ — that too is its mitzva — so that they do not exclude drawing back and forth
